link.title: LaTeX Equation on Multiple Lines: align, split, multline

entry.summary: To put a LaTeX equation on multiple lines, wrap the lines in an environment: align* (or aligned inside \[ … \]) when the equals signs should line up, gather* when each line is simply centred, multline* for one formula too long for a line. entry.title: Overleaf to Google Docs™: Chapters, .bib and Figures

link.title: Overleaf to Google Docs™: Chapters, .bib and Figures

entry.summary: Overleaf cannot export to Google Docs™, so to move an Overleaf project into Docs you download its source as a .zip and import the .tex from it. LaTeXFlow Import writes the headings, lists, tables and equations into the document; the .bib file and the figures from the same .zip go in with two short steps of their own.
